subject: Custody modeling: dedicated vs private economic scenarios
messages:
From: Anna Rios <anna.rios@covellhealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@covellhealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Custody requirements and sizing questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Covell's security team needs a clear economic comparison between Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) and a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem with custody controls) for our PHI workloads.

High-level asks:
- Target QPS: 45 peak concurrent low-latency streams (95th pctl latency <250ms) for NLP inference, primarily short-document summarization.
- Data custody: all model inputs and logs must remain inside Covell's VPC; audit logs retained for 7 years.
- Contract horizon: 18 months with an option to expand.

Can you send a scenario-driven cost model and a short playbook for procurement/ops tradeoffs? Procurement copied for timeline alignment.

Cheers,
Anna
Anna Rios
Head of AI Ops, Covell Health

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anna Rios <anna.rios@covellhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Custody requirements and sizing questions

Anna — thanks for the clear requirements. High level yes, we can support both hosting postures but the economics and operational responsibilities differ.

I attached a first-pass capacity model (covell_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) and a short cost breakdown (redwood_cost_breakdown_q4.pdf). Quick summary up front:
- Dedicated: lower ops overhead for Covell, faster time-to-live, predictable per-token pricing. Expect 20-25% lower up-front integration effort but requires commitment for reserved GPU capacity to hit the lowest unit rates.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): higher initial setup (networking, KMS, audit pipeline), higher fixed infra cost, but gives Covell direct control over custody and audit retention. Better for customers who require HSM integration or on-prem air-gapped lanes.

Key variables I modeled: average request length (tokens), KV cache hit rate, batching headroom, and required GPU tiling to support 45 concurrent streams at 95th pctl latency target. In the workbook I included three capacity scenarios (conservative / expected / optimized).

Next steps: Marissa, Rishi — can you review the capacity tiling sheets and confirm assumptions for model variants and quantization options? Anna, procurement, if useful we can draft a short SOW to align responsibilities (ops, network, audit).

Regards,
Vivek
Head of Global Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: covell_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Rios <anna.rios@covellhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Custody requirements and sizing questions

Vivek — reviewed and added conservative GPU-tiling assumptions. See notes in sheet 'tiling_notes'. Summary changes:
- For conservative scenario I recommend reserving a mix of A10G-equivalent instances for steady baseline and 20% burst capacity on p4d-style instances behind autoscale. This hybrid keeps per-token cost reasonable while meeting 95th pctl SLAs.
- For the private VPC option, include an ops uplift of 12-18% to account for network egress design, encryption key sync, and audit pipeline maintenance.

Anna — two procurement questions:
1) Will Covell accept encrypted logs forwarded to your S3 with lifecycle rules, or do you require HSM-backed local retention?
2) Any preferred cloud region for the VPC footprint? (we modeled us-west-2 and us-east-1 in the workbook)

I'll prepare a short one-page runbook that maps handoffs (Redwood ops vs Covell infra) and a recommended SOW outline for Marissa/Vivek to share with procurement.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Rios <anna.rios@covellhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@covellhealth.com, David Keller <david.keller@alpha-consulting.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Custody requirements and sizing questions

Marissa — thanks, that hybrid recommendation looks promising. Answers to your procurement questions:
1) We prefer HSM-backed retention for the master audit keys and local retention for primary logs for compliance right now. Forwarding encrypted logs to Covell S3 can be a backup, but the primary copy must be under our key control.
2) Region: us-east-1 preferred for latency to our application.

David (copied) is our external infra consultant; he'll help validate the SOW and procurement timeline. Procurement, our goal is to finalize hosting posture within the next 3 weeks so we can lock capacity for the pilot.

Anna

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anna Rios <anna.rios@covellhealth.com>, procurement@covellhealth.com

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Custody requirements and sizing questions

Great — alignment on HSM and us-east-1 noted. Action plan and asks below:

1) Redwood will: prepare a 1-page SOW draft and a final cost scenario (conservative/expected/optimized) with explicit breakout for: reserved capacity amortization, burst pool costs, ops uplift for private VPC, and one-time integration fees.
2) Covell: confirm target QPS distribution (peak hour vs typical) and confirm whether audit logs must remain immutable inside your VPC or if write-once S3 with locks is acceptable.
3) Timeline: Aim to exchange the SOW and final pricing by Wed Nov 24. To hit this we need Covell feedback on the two items above by Mon Nov 22.

Attached: SOW-draft-Covell.docx (template with roles/responsibilities). I'll loop Legal after procurement confirms posture so we can expedite terms for reserved capacity.

Thanks all — Rishi and Karthik will be on standby for any technical deep dives next week.

Best,
Vivek
